items.title: AI chip price-performance grew ~49% per year since 2023, doubling every 1.7 years
items.summary_en: Epoch AI's AI Chip Sales Hub data insight reports that the performance-per-dollar of AI chips purchased each quarter has grown by an average of 49% per year (90% CI: 36-66%/year) since 2023, in constant 2025 dollars. Epoch AI states the gains arrive in spurts tied to generational shifts in spending rather than smooth continuous improvement — price-performance was nearly flat through mid-2024, then roughly doubled as Blackwell-generation chips became a majority of new purchases.
items.notes: Epoch AI itself states a wide 90% confidence interval (36-66%/year), reflecting significant estimation uncertainty. Growth is described as lumpy/generation-driven rather than steady, per Epoch's own framing. Could not verify full methodology text directly due to network access block on epoch.ai in this session.

items.title: Will financing bottleneck AI compute? An Anthropic case study
items.summary_en: Epoch AI published a case study examining Anthropic's ~$50 billion compute infrastructure commitment (announced November 2025), including roughly $35 billion in debt to purchase TPU systems, structured with Broadcom, Apollo, and Blackstone. Epoch AI argues that, based on this case, financing is unlikely to be an immediate bottleneck to frontier AI compute growth, and suggests later deployments could become larger and cheaper to finance as investors grow more comfortable with the asset class.
items.notes: Epoch AI explicitly frames this as a single-company case study (Anthropic only); generalizing the conclusion to other labs' financing arrangements is an extrapolation, not something Epoch AI claims to have verified broadly. Full original text not directly fetched due to network block on epochai.substack.com; summary based on indexed search snippets of Epoch's own page.
